subject: general
question: Which of the following statements regarding an atom is correct?

options.text: An atom does not contain any positive charge
Atoms as a whole are electrically neutral

solution:
The correct answer is __**Atoms as a whole are electrically neutral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An atom is composed of three primary subatomic particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons.
 
• Protons carry a positive charge, electrons carry a negative charge, and neutrons are neutral.
 
• The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is equal to the number of electrons surrounding the nucleus, making the atom electrically neutral overall.
 
• The positive charges of protons are balanced by the negative charges of electrons.
 
• If an atom gains or loses electrons, it becomes an ion and is no longer electrically neutral.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protons**

 
 
• Protons are positively charged subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons defines the element and its atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Neutrons**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral subatomic particles also found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They contribute to the atomic mass but do not affect the atomic charge.
 
 
 
• **Electrons**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged subatomic particles that orbit the nucleus of an atom in electron shells.
 
• The arrangement of electrons determines the chemical properties and reactivity of the element.
